options.A: Permanent stiffening of the peripheral joints
options.B: Immediate infection of the superficial skin layers
options.C: Rapid development of severe seasonal allergies
options.D: Massive internal bleeding without visible external wounds

explanation: A person can look fine on the outside while bleeding heavily inside. That's why careful, hands-on nursing assessment is always key! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h2)

question: How do collected incident reports directly help improve hospital quality?

options.A: By ensuring the hospital meets strict interior cleaning schedules
options.B: By providing evidence to lower the salaries of underperforming staff
options.C: By revealing recurring error trends that guide workflow changes
options.D: By allowing administrators to reduce the number of working nurses

explanation: Spot on! Reviewing multiple reports together highlights patterns, helping managers fix root problems across the whole hospital. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h8)

question: What is the main cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Gradual resistance of body cells to normal insulin
options.C: Temporary hormone changes during pregnancy
options.D: Poor dietary intake of refined carbohydrates

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks the insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Brilliant to keep this distinction in mind! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main danger associated with postpartum hemorrhage in new mothers?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to walk
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to routine food
options.C: Chronic high blood pressure lasting years
options.D: Sudden and severe blood loss leading to shock

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage involves heavy bleeding after birth, which can quickly drop blood pressure and cause life-threatening shock if untreated. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why must nurses keep reassessing patients who have already been sorted into a triage category?

options.A: Rescue teams need to change patient names frequently
options.B: Color tags often fall off in wet weather conditions
options.C: Hospital admission clerks require updated paperwork every hour
options.D: A patient's condition can rapidly deteriorate over time

explanation: Exactly! Injuries can hide beneath the surface, meaning a patient who looks stable now could crash and need urgent help a few minutes later. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the underlying physiological problem in all types of shock?

options.A: Chronic inflammation of the joints
options.B: Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular hypoxia
options.C: An excess of oxygen in the circulating blood
options.D: A sudden increase in overall body temperature

explanation: Shock occurs when cells do not receive enough oxygen-rich blood to perform normal metabolism. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the main physiological purpose of dietary proteins in the body?

options.A: Maintaining rapid nerve conduction and fluid balance
options.B: Tissue growth, hormone synthesis, and immune defense
options.C: Providing a dense energy reserve for long-term fasting
options.D: Acting as a solvent for fat-soluble vitamins

explanation: Proteins are made of amino acids that build and repair tissues, create vital enzymes and hormones, and support immune function. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of a psychiatric nurse in a CBR program?

options.A: Ordering all medical supplies directly from international factories
options.B: Managing the financial budget of the national ministry of health
options.C: Constructing physical buildings for local primary health centers
options.D: Monitoring medication compliance and watching for signs of relapse

explanation: Nurses regularly check if clients are taking their drugs correctly and observe for early behavioral changes that indicate the illness might be returning. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why must pregnant women avoid eating raw or undercooked meats?

options.A: Raw meat causes severe allergic skin rashes in expectant mothers
options.B: Because cooked meat has more protein than raw meat
options.C: To prevent dangerous foodborne infections that can harm the pregnancy
options.D: Undercooked meat takes much longer for the stomach to digest

explanation: Raw meat can hide tricky germs and parasites like toxoplasma. Cooking food thoroughly keeps both mum and baby safe from infections! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h4)

question: Why is adequate iron intake particularly crucial immediately following childbirth and during lactation?

options.A: To help the infant digest complex carbohydrates in the milk
options.B: To stimulate the mammary glands to produce more milk volume
options.C: To prevent postpartum anemia and recover from blood loss during delivery
options.D: To regulate the mother's blood pressure during night feeds

explanation: Childbirth involves blood loss, and iron helps build new red blood cells to keep the mother strong and energized. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h4)

question: Why don't we diagnose someone with high blood pressure (hypertension) after just one high reading?

options.A: Nigerian guidelines require at least five months of tracking
options.B: Blood pressure machines only work accurately on the third try
options.C: Systolic pressure changes constantly based on what food was eaten
options.D: Temporary factors like stress or rushing can falsely raise readings

explanation: Things like rushing to the clinic, traffic anxiety, or pain can make BP jump temporarily. That's why we always check a few times before making a diagnosis. Great job thinking like a nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h1)

question: A patient refuses a bath because the bathroom feels cold and confusing. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with personal hygiene
options.B: Cancel all future baths indefinitely to avoid upsetting the patient
options.C: Warm the room, simplify the process, and break it down into gentle steps
options.D: Force the patient into the tub immediately to maintain hygiene standards

explanation: Making the environment cozy and taking things slow helps ease fear and resistance during personal care. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT safe for staff working in the TSSU decontamination zone?

options.A: Putting on face shields and eye protection
options.B: Wearing waterproof protective aprons
options.C: Wearing open-toed sandals for comfort
options.D: Using heavy-duty utility gloves

explanation: Great catch! Open-toed shoes leave your feet exposed to falling sharps and dirty splashes. Always wear closed, protective shoes in the wash area! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why do patients taking lithium need careful guidance about their salt and water intake?

options.A: Salt completely destroys the chemical structure of the lithium pill
options.B: Lithium alters fluid balance and can easily reach toxic levels if hydration shifts
options.C: Water causes lithium to instantly evaporate inside the human stomach
options.D: Patients on lithium lose all sense of taste for salty foods

explanation: Spot on! Lithium handles similarly to sodium in the kidneys, so dehydration or sudden salt changes can dangerously spike drug levels. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: What actually happens in heart valve stenosis?

options.A: An infection develops on the inner lining of the heart
options.B: The valve opening narrows and makes it hard for blood to push through
options.C: The valve flaps fail to close tightly, letting blood leak backward
options.D: The heart valve fails to form at all before birth

explanation: Stenosis means narrowing. A stenotic valve is stiff and tight, making the heart push extra hard to get blood through the opening. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of DRF exemptions in healthcare facilities?

options.A: To punish patients who refuse to pay hospital bills
options.B: To increase the daily revenue of the drug fund
options.C: To provide a financial safety net for vulnerable patients
options.D: To help the hospital pharmacy clear out expired drugs

explanation: Think of exemptions as a safety cushion designed to protect patients who truly cannot afford the cost of their medications. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h2)

question: How often should you remind families to change the batteries in their smoke alarms?

options.A: Every ten years
options.B: At least once a year
options.C: Only when the fire department visits
options.D: Every two weeks

explanation: Fresh batteries save lives! Changing them at least once a year ensures the smoke detector will actually sound when an emergency happens. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T8#GNS324_U6_T8_h5)

question: After cigarette smoking, what is recognized as the second leading cause of lung cancer?

options.A: Radon gas exposure
options.B: Asbestos inhalation
options.C: Secondhand tobacco smoke
options.D: Airborne coal dust

explanation: Spot on! Radon is a natural radioactive gas that can build up in buildings. After smoking, it's the next big culprit behind lung cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: How does health insurance make it easier for people to get medical care?

options.A: By making all drugs and lab tests completely free to manufacture
options.B: By making it so hospitals no longer need to hire nurses
options.C: By pooling money together so the cost is shared across a large group of people
options.D: By ensuring that no one with insurance will ever catch a chronic illness

explanation: Brilliant! Insurance works like a cooperative contribution—everyone chips in a little so that when someone falls sick, the heavy bill is easily paid from the shared pool. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h4)

question: What goes wrong if you crush an extended-release capsule before giving it to a patient?

options.A: The medication will take twice as long to work
options.B: The entire dose is released at once, risking toxicity
options.C: The patient will experience no therapeutic effect
options.D: The active ingredients are completely destroyed

explanation: Crushing destroys the special timed-release design. Instead of a steady, safe trickle of medicine over hours, the patient gets a dangerous flood all at once! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h2)

question: What can happen if a nursing research study uses a sample size that is far too small?

options.A: The statistical software will refuse to run any calculations
options.B: Every patient in the hospital will be forced to participate
options.C: The researcher might miss a real and important clinical effect
options.D: The study will automatically cost too much money to complete

explanation: Spot on! If your group of patients is too tiny, your study won't have enough power to spot a real pattern or treatment benefit. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h5)

question: What is a major physical risk when a young, physically immature teenager gets pregnant?

options.A: Rapid muscle expansion
options.B: Obstructed labor
options.C: Excessive bone density
options.D: Enhanced fetal growth

explanation: Spot on! An adolescent's pelvis may not be fully grown yet, which can cause serious complications like obstructed labor during childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h6)

question: How is a nursing diagnosis different from a medical diagnosis?

options.A: A medical diagnosis describes how a patient feels emotionally
options.B: A nursing diagnosis focuses on how the patient responds to health conditions
options.C: A medical diagnosis can only be made by a registered nurse
options.D: A nursing diagnosis identifies the exact pathology of a disease

explanation: You've got this! A medical diagnosis names the disease itself (like malaria), while a nursing diagnosis focuses on how the patient reacts to it (like feeling exhausted or in pain). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h3)

question: How do global health organizations view female genital mutilation?

options.A: As an acceptable traditional surgical option
options.B: As a violation of basic human rights
options.C: As a mandatory rite of passage for health
options.D: As a minor procedure with minimal complications

explanation: Correct! Major health bodies view FGM as a serious violation of human rights and bodily safety for women and girls. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h1)

question: A community nurse teaches schoolgirls how to maintain personal hygiene during menstruation. What is the main goal here?

options.A: To test the students on complex biological terminology
options.B: To replace traditional family guidance with strict hospital rules
options.C: To build self-reliance and prevent preventable reproductive infections
options.D: To ensure the school pays a consulting fee to the local clinic

explanation: Wonderful! Teaching self-care gives young people the practical knowledge they need to protect their health independently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h6)

question: In aeromedical work, what does the safety acronym 'CRM' stand for?

options.A: Certified Rescue Medic
options.B: Crew Resource Management
options.C: Clinical Risk Method
options.D: Critical Respiratory Monitoring

explanation: You've got this! CRM is a fantastic aviation safety framework that encourages teamwork, clear communication, and shared problem-solving among everyone on board. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T14#GNS321_U2_T14_h8)

question: Why is it so important for the immune system to tell the difference between 'self' and 'non-self'?

options.A: It prevents the immune system from attacking healthy host tissues
options.B: It ensures that nutrients are absorbed properly in the intestines
options.C: It helps the body maintain a stable internal core temperature
options.D: It allows red blood cells to carry more oxygen to organs

explanation: Knowing what belongs to the body ('self') stops the immune system from mistakenly attacking healthy organs and tissues—which is what happens in autoimmune diseases! [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why does patient awareness nowadays push nursing practice to improve?

options.A: Patients expect safe, high-quality, and evidence-based care
options.B: Patients refuse to interact with newly graduated nurses
options.C: Patients prefer traditional remedies over hospital treatment
options.D: Patients demand complete control over hospital budgeting

explanation: Exactly! As people become more informed about their health rights, nurses step up their game to deliver safer, top-notch care. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when conducting community health education?

options.A: Involving respected local leaders in the mobilization
options.B: Addressing local cultural beliefs respectfully
options.C: Using complex medical jargon to impress the audience
options.D: Communicating in the primary language of the community

explanation: Using complicated clinical terms confuses people and creates a barrier to learning, which is why simple language is essential. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h7)

question: How does drug absorption in the lower rectum affect metabolism?

options.C: It forces the drug to be stored in the kidneys
options.D: It bypasses the liver's first-pass metabolism

question: What is the main sign that a medical situation is a true life-threatening emergency?

options.C: Immediate failure of one or more vital organ systems
options.D: A chronic condition that lasts longer than six months

question: A patient has damage to their cochlea and auditory nerve. What type of hearing loss is this?

options.A: Sensorineural hearing loss
options.B: Central processing loss
options.C: Mixed hearing loss
options.D: Conductive hearing loss

explanation: When the inner ear structures (like the cochlea) or the hearing nerve itself are damaged, we call it sensorineural hearing loss. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T14#GNS324_U4_T14_h3)

question: In the SMART goal framework, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Meaningful
options.B: Methodical
options.C: Manual
options.D: Measurable

question: Which dietary combination helps your body absorb non-heme (plant-based) iron better?

options.D: Iron with Vitamin C

question: What is the classic sign that a patient has entered the prodromal stage of an infection?

options.A: Vague feelings of tiredness and mild body discomfort

options.C: Full-blown paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Complete recovery of normal daily energy levels

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of HIV orphans?

options.A: People assume all orphans are infected with HIV themselves

options.C: People think orphans are immune to childhood malnutrition

question: A resident suddenly becomes confused and restless. What should you suspect first instead of brushing it off as normal aging?

options.C: A normal and expected part of getting older
options.D: An acute problem like delirium caused by an infection

question: What should you tell a patient who has a normal routine EEG result, but a clear history of seizures?

options.A: The patient's seizures have spontaneously resolved without medical intervention
options.B: A normal EEG does not rule out epilepsy because abnormal waves may not occur during a short test
options.C: The testing equipment was likely calibrated incorrectly during the procedure
options.D: Further neurological evaluation is unnecessary once a normal EEG is recorded

question: Why is asking about the last menstrual period crucial during an emergency contraception assessment?

question: Which type of ovarian cancer is the most common, making up about 90% of all cases?

question: Why are human carriers tricky when it comes to spreading infections?

options.C: They are completely immune to all known antibiotics
options.D: They always require emergency intensive care

explanation: Carriers look and feel totally fine, which is why we practice standard precautions with everyone—germs can hide where we least expect them! [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does the term 'polyspermy' mean?

options.C: The total failure of ovulation to occur in a cycle
options.D: The premature breakdown of the zona pellucida

question: How does mentorship from a unit manager help newly qualified nurses?

options.A: It exempts them from working night shifts
options.B: It guarantees they will never make a clinical mistake
options.C: It helps them transition from students to confident practitioners
options.D: It allows them to bypass hospital safety protocols

explanation: Exactly! Stepping out of the classroom and onto the ward can feel scary. Good mentorship gives new nurses the guidance and boost they need to feel confident. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h2)

question: If a clinic is installing new digital monitors in every patient room, what must be checked first?

options.C: The total number of parking spaces available for incoming visitors

question: What is the permanent adult name for the leftover, closed-up ductus venosus inside the liver?

question: When is epidemiologic data considered fully utilised in public health?

options.A: When it drives practical action and health interventions
options.B: When it is printed in a foreign medical textbook
options.C: When field logbooks are completely filled with ink
options.D: When it is locked away safely in a government vault

explanation: Data exists to guide decision-making and solve real community health problems, not just sit on a shelf. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h6)

question: How is mifepristone normally given in a standard abortion protocol?

question: Why is directing considered more than just giving orders?

options.D: It focuses only on punishing staff who make mistakes

question: Two hours after a colonoscopy, a patient's abdomen feels hard like a board and they have severe pain. What should you do first?

question: Which everyday or routine activity carries a real risk of transmitting HIV?

options.C: Receiving a hug or handshake from an infected coworker

explanation: HIV spreads through direct blood-to-blood contact, such as sharing needles. Casual contact like hugging or sharing spoons is completely safe! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which symptom is most common for a small, simple ovarian cyst?

question: When should the nurse document the findings and actions of a home visit?

options.D: Whenever the supervisor remembers to ask for it

question: A patient complains of a stubborn dry cough two weeks after starting a new blood pressure pill. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all medications immediately without telling anyone

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.D: Monitoring is done by villagers, while evaluation is done by politicians

question: What does the ethical principle of autonomy mean for an older patient?

options.A: The duty of the nurse to do no harm
options.B: The obligation to tell the truth at all times
options.C: The fair distribution of medical resources
options.D: The right to make their own healthcare decisions

question: A patient keeps asking you to check their blood pressure and look at a tiny skin mark. What is the best first nursing action?

options.B: Tell the patient firmly that their behavior is foolish and they need to stop worrying

question: Why is maintaining strict medical confidentiality so crucial in reproductive health nursing?

options.A: It protects client privacy and preserves trust in the nurse
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not interfere with nursing duties
options.C: It prevents the government from tracking birth rates
options.D: It reduces the administrative paperwork required by the hospital

question: What type of clothing is best for someone working outdoors in areas with lots of stinging insects?

options.B: Shorts and sleeveless tops to stay cool in the heat
options.C: Light-colored, long-sleeved clothing that fits smoothly
options.D: Dark wool garments to absorb sweat effectively

explanation: You got it! Smooth, light-covered, long clothes protect your skin and help you avoid attracting insects that love dark colors and floral patterns. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h8)

question: Why do nurses join trade unions and professional associations?

options.B: To diagnose patients without consulting medical doctors
options.C: To collectively advocate for better working conditions and pay

options.D: Collect a clean-catch urine sample to check for sugar and protein

question: What is the main underlying cause of osteoarthritis?

question: A hospitalized patient with chronic bronchitis is struggling to breathe and their oxygen is dropping. What should the nurse do FIRST?
